reports.title: Loi n°012-2018/AN du 07 mai 2018 portant modification de la loi n°055-2004/AN du 21 décembre 2004 portant Code Général des Collectivités Territoriales au Burkina Faso
reports.description: The 2018 amendment instrument to the 2004 CGCT, retrieved directly from the Assemblée Nationale's own site (landing page https://www.assembleenationale.bf/loip/343). NOT a full consolidated CGCT text — a short, 2-article instrument amending only Articles 173 and 252 of the 2004 code (special-delegation/dissolution rules for regional and municipal councils). Title block: "LOI N°012-2018/AN PORTANT MODIFICATION DE LA LOI N°055-2004/AN DU 21 DECEMBRE 2004 PORTANT CODE GENERAL DES COLLECTIVITES TERRITORIALES AU BURKINA FASO." Adoption clause: "a délibéré en sa séance du 07 mai 2018 et adopté la loi dont la teneur suit." Article 1 substitutes a new Art. 173 governing repeated council-dissolution crises: "En cas de crise répétée entrainant pour le même conseil une seconde dissolution, la démission de tous les membres en exercice ou l'annulation devenue définitive de l'élection de tous ses membres, il est procédé, pour le reste du mandat, à l'installation d'une délégation spéciale présidée par le représentant de l'Etat dans les conditions fixées par décret pris en Conseil des ministres," and a new Art. 252 extending the same rule to arrondissement councils in communes à statut particulier: "Dans le cas des communes à statut particulier, les mêmes dispositions de dissolution s'appliquent aux conseils d'arrondissement. Dans ce cas, la présidence de la délégation spéciale est assurée par un représentant de l'Etat nommé par arrêté du ministre en charge des collectivités territoriales." Article 2 is an explicit repeal clause naming two intermediate amendment laws it supersedes: "La présente loi qui abroge toutes les dispositions antérieures contraires notamment celles des lois n°016-2015/CNT du 21 mai 2015 et n°027-2017/AN du 18 mai 2017, sera exécutée comme loi de l'Etat." CAVEAT: this is governance/dissolution content, not fiscal/budget content directly — filed under municipal-finance because it amends the same foundational collectivités-territoriales code (bf-loi-055-2004-cgct) that carries this corpus's municipal-finance regime (Titre II, Articles 106-121), and because council dissolution/special-delegation rules bear on fiscal continuity (who exercises budgetary authority when a council is dissolved), even though this specific amendment's own text does not itself state a budget figure.

dependencies.basis: This law's own title block and body name and modify the 2004 code by number and article: it is titled a modification of "la loi n°055-2004/AN du 21 décembre 2004 portant Code Général des Collectivités Territoriales au Burkina Faso," and Article 1 states it substitutes new text for named articles of that code (Art. 173 and Art. 252). An explicit amendment relationship to a specific named predecessor instrument.

_dropped.edge: Loi n°016-2015/CNT du 21 mai 2015 (named/repealed by Loi n°012-2018/AN's Article 2) -> full primary text
_dropped.why: Confirmed to exist and to be a genuine prior amendment to the 2004 CGCT — named explicitly in bf-loi-012-2018-cgct-amendment's own Article 2 repeal clause ("...notamment celles des lois n°016-2015/CNT du 21 mai 2015 et n°027-2017/AN du 18 mai 2017"). Located on NATLEX, but as an image-only scanned PDF with zero extractable text — a genuine 'published but not machine-readable' case, not a confirmed absence. Would need an OCR pass to responsibly mint; not attempted this round. Flagged as a future OCR candidate. (Loi n°027-2017/AN, the other law named in the same repeal clause, was not located at all this round and is a separate, unresearched lead.)

The reported wholesale CGCT replacement adopted 30 December 2025 by the Assemblée Législative de Transition (per MATD's own site) is NOT a new finding this round — it is already minted in this corpus as bf-alt-cgct-2025-adoption (in af-burkina-faso-national-deepen.json), which already carries its own caveat that the news coverage was WebFetch-summarized rather than independently verbatim-verified and that the new law's own number was not given in the sources checked. No new _dropped 'deferred' lead is added here to avoid duplicating that existing lead; a future round should chase the new code's actual number/text via MATD or ALT sources and, once found, would supersede both bf-loi-055-2004-cgct and this 2018 amendment node. No citation text was found this round establishing a direct textual link between the 2018 amendment and the 2025 replacement (unsurprising, since the 2025 replacement postdates this round's primary source and the 2018 law obviously cannot cite something 7 years in its future) — no edge is asserted between them.

_dropped.edge: bf-loi-012-2018-cgct-amendment (or a new AES-exposé-des-motifs node) -> AES/CEDEAO-withdrawal exposé des motifs (an.bf, ratification of the Charte du Liptako-Gourma)
_dropped.why: A genuine Burkina Faso primary source was surfaced this round (via a Mali research thread): the Assemblée Nationale du Burkina Faso's own exposé des motifs for the bill ratifying the Charte du Liptako-Gourma instituting the AES (https://www.an.bf/storage/libelexpomotif/Bx8Fr4ipqjH5owqlCfshzy6dyVSuDf00azKcxWZJ.pdf), which documents in Burkina's own voice the CEDEAO-withdrawal rationale following the July 2023 Niger coup, and names both Burkina Faso and Mali. This is political/foreign-policy content (AES founding, ECOWAS withdrawal rationale, mutual-defense framing), not economic or fiscal content, and has no citation link to this round's municipal-finance/CGCT-amendment work. Judged out of scope for this economic/fiscal-focused project and not minted as a node. Recorded here so it is not re-discovered from scratch if the project's scope broadens to external-action/regional-cooperation content — the `external-action` domain already exists in the schema and bf-mof-aes-cedeao-2024 (Burkina's Ministry of Finance's own AES/CEDEAO coverage) is already a node in af-burkina-faso-national-deepen.json, so a future round minting this exposé des motifs would likely cite or be cited alongside that existing node.
